title: Saag Aloo
subtitle: Spiced potatoes and spinach
excerpt: Saag aloo pairs soft, golden potatoes with wilted spinach in a simple spiced base. It works as a side dish alongside dal or curry, or as a light main with flatbreads. The mustard seeds add a faint nuttiness that lifts the whole dish.
sourceNotes: Saag aloo is a staple across the Punjab and northern India, where saag refers broadly to leafy greens. The combination of mustard seeds and cumin bloomed in hot oil is a foundational technique in South Asian cooking.

content.text: Cut the potatoes to a consistent size so they cook evenly. A 2 cm cube takes around 15 minutes with a lid on; larger pieces will need more time.

Heat the sunflower oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. When it shimmers, add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds. As soon as the mustard seeds start to pop, add the onion and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook the onion for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin-ground, and chilli flakes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Add the potato cubes and stir to coat in the spice base. Pour in the tinned tomatoes and 200 ml of water. Season with salt, cover with a lid, and cook for 15 minutes until the potatoes are almost tender.
Remove the lid and add the spinach in three or four batches, stirring each batch in until wilted before adding the next.
Once all the spinach has wilted and the potatoes are fully cooked through, stir in the garam masala. Taste, adjust seasoning, and serve.

items.symptom: The potatoes are still hard after 15 minutes
items.cause: The cubes may be too large, or the pan was not covered tightly
items.fix: Ensure the lid is on firmly and add another splash of water. Cook in 5-minute increments until a knife slides in cleanly.

items.symptom: The spinach has made the dish watery
items.cause: Spinach releases a lot of liquid as it wilts
items.fix: Remove the lid and cook over medium heat for a few minutes to evaporate the excess liquid.
